title: Usage telemetry is opt-in, counts only operator actions, and a serving process never uploads
scope:
how the project measures that Novis is actually used — the two consents, the counter
schema, when a payload may leave the machine and from which process shapes, `nvs update-check`'s
output contract, the endpoint's configurability, and when this is implemented. Not in scope: package
updating — `nvs update` is [0081](0081.md)'s resolver
and this ADR's version check is deliberately spelled `update-check` so the two never collide; the
server's response headers and proxy contract ([0097](0097.md));
a Novis *application's* metrics and tracing ([0076](0076.md)); user code's
outbound-request policy ([0058](0058.md)), which governs the language, not
the tool.

summary.headline: Telemetry is off by default, and a process serving traffic never uploads
summary.body:
Two switches, both off until the operator turns them on: usage telemetry and the update check.
Each `nvs` command then adds one to a local counter for the subcommand that ran, never its
arguments and never anything about the requests a server handled. At most once a week the
previous week's totals ride along with a short command, commonly the update check. A serving
process only counts; it never uploads. An upload cannot fail the command carrying it, and `nvs
telemetry show` prints what would be sent.
